1.pericope_label: Then Jonah prayed unto the Lord his God out of the fish’s belly
debates: Whether the prayer was uttered in the fish or afterwards on land
How a man could pray or breathe in such a place
What the belly of hell means
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch reads the whole as thanksgiving for a deliverance already pledged rather than a petition for one
Ellicott would drop the connecting word before thou heardest, since the abrupt change of person is the stronger figure
themes: A quarrel begun on one side and healed from the other
A man who could not face the God he was fleeing
Freedom of access inside a dark dungeon
Past tenses marking a prayer that never stopped

3.pericope_label: For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods compassed me about
debates: Why the casting into the sea is ascribed to God and not the sailors
Whether being cast out of sight leaves any faith standing
Whether the last clause is a resolve or a refusal
outliers: Clarke reads the billows passing over as a literal description of the sea above the swimming fish
Calvin answers the charge that despair extinguishes faith by making the conflict itself the trial of faith
themes: A man who will not blame the hands that threw him
Pronouns fixed on God and not on the crew
One thought met by its opposite
A temple still standing to look toward

5.pericope_label: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul: the depth closed me round about, the weeds were wrapped about my head
debates: Whether the weeds and the mountains are literal or the figure of a drowning man
What even to the soul means
Whether the bars are those of the earth or of the under-world
outliers: Ellicott points out that the fish is never mentioned anywhere in the poem, and takes the whole as a picture of drowning
Clarke supposes the prayer was drafted in the fish and afterwards worked into verse with clauses added
themes: Seaweed swallowed as food by the creature
Hills whose foundations are planted in the sea
The whole earth serving as one door
A rescue described as a resurrection

7.pericope_label: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple
debates: What the fainting of the soul describes
Who the observers of lying vanities are
What forsaking their own mercy costs them
outliers: Calvin keeps the root sense of the verb and reads that the soul rolled itself up, against the usual rendering of failing
Gill turns the proverb back on Jonah himself rather than on idolaters or on the ship crew
themes: A mist of death stealing over the senses
Thoughts that recoil on the man who has them
Prayer sent out as a messenger to a temple
A covenant privilege that can be forfeited

9.pericope_label: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord
debates: What kind of sacrifice is promised
What weight the word spake carries
Whether the whole account can be read without a miracle
outliers: Clarke sets out a rationalising reading that makes the fish a fishing creek, and rejects it as denying both the sign and the thing signified
Calvin counts several distinct miracles in the escape rather than one
themes: Praise offered alongside a legal sacrifice
A conviction held as a bond against new superstition
A creature that could not keep its prisoner
A grave opened on the third day
